subject: Orchard private GPU deployment — bandwidth right-sizing, SLO alignment, and predictive scale thresholds

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@orchardhealth.com>

Subject: Orchard private GPU deployment — initial bandwidth & SLA questions

Hi Sergio / Marissa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this week. We’re starting to map the private VPC deployment into our networking and SRE plans and have a few early questions so we can feed accurate numbers into procurement and capacity tooling. High-level asks below — we copied a rough network diagram and a first-pass capacity sheet (attached).

Key goals (what Orchard needs):
- 99th-percentile tail latency <= 750ms for interactive routing (user-facing chat) under sustained 800 QPS bursts.
- Bound monthly egress cost to $12k (initial budget) across all regions.
- Plan for graceful degradation when GPU headroom < 20% (policy: model fallback to 8-bit quantized variant).

Questions we need your help with:
1) How do you typically size private GPU clusters for a customer-specified 99p latency SLO vs sustained QPS? What margin factors do you recommend for on-prem switches and NIC contention?
2) Does Redwood offer packet shaping/egress rate limiting at the edge so we can cap token emission during surges? If so, how configurable is the throttle (per-tenant, per-route)?
3) For predictive scaling: what telemetry should we export from our ingress (latency, queue depth, tokens/sec) to get accurate scale decisions? Any recommended thresholds to trigger a warm-up?

Attachments: orchard_privdeploy_network_diagram.pdf (network diagram), capacity_model_v1.xlsx (working sheet).

Happy to jump on a short call next week to run numbers together.

Best,
Elaine Park
Director, Platform Operations
Orchard Health

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@orchardhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Orchard private GPU deployment — initial bandwidth & SLA questions

Elaine — thanks for the detail and the attachments, very helpful. Short answers up front, then a sketch of the sizing approach we’d use so your SRE/procurement team can validate numbers.

TL;DR answers:
- Sizing approach: convert SLA into steady-state tokens/sec requirement by multiplying expected QPS * avg tokens per request and adding headroom margin (we typically use 1.3x for sustained workloads and 1.6x for spiky workloads).
- Packet shaping: yes, Redwood Private supports per-route soft throttles and token-budgeting at the VPC edge. You can enforce both token/sec caps and burst windows.
- Telemetry for predictive scaling: ingest request QPS, 95/99 tail latency, GPU utilization, and request token length histogram. Trigger warm-up when 95p latency > target OR queued requests / warm-pool capacity > 0.2.

Sizing sketch (quick numbers using your targets):
- Target steady sustained burst: 800 QPS (interactive).
- Assumed avg tokens per request: 450 tokens (please confirm).
- Tokens/sec = 800 * 450 = 360k tok/s.
- We map tok/s to GPU capacity using model profile: e.g., og-16b FP16 baseline processes ~50 tok/s per GPU (depends on sequence length). For 360k tok/s you’d need ~7200 GPU-seconds of compute per second -> this is wrong phrasing; better to think in GPUs: 360k tok/s / 50 tok/s per GPU = 7200 GPUs (this signals mismatch—see note).

Important callout: the per-GPU token/s figure varies wildly by model and sequence length; 50 tok/s is a conservative single-stream baseline for large 16B models on older cards. Practical optimization levers: batching, KV cache reuse, quantized variants (x8/x4), and multiplexing. With batching + 4x quantization and prefix caching we often reduce effective tok/s per-GPU cost by 6-10x. That changes the math dramatically.

Next steps proposal:
1) Marissa and I will take the capacity_model_v1.xlsx and run two scenarios (conservative, optimized) based on the model families you plan to use.
2) Can you confirm the average sequence length and ratio of chat vs stateless completion?
3) We’ll propose: initial private pool with a warm-pool of N GPUs, a scaling policy that adds M GPUs when a 2m rolling 95p latency breaches 650ms, and per-route throttles that cap token emit to X tok/s during graceful-deg.

I’ll include a worked example in a follow-up once Marissa runs the model profiles.

—Sergio
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai, Elaine Park <elaine.park@orchardhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Jul 2026 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orchard private GPU deployment — initial bandwidth & SLA questions

Elaine, Sergio — I ran the quick-probe in the attached workbook and added two model profiles in the sheet "model_profiles" (opt-16b-quantized, opt-30b-fp16). A few clarifications and concrete numbers below.

Assumptions I used (please update):
- Chat vs completion ratio: 70% chat (avg 480 tokens), 30% stateless (avg 200 tokens).
- Weighted avg tokens per request (chat weighted): 0.7*480 + 0.3*200 = 416 tok/request.
- Effective tok/s per GPU baseline (FP16, batched, NVLink, Ampere+):
  - opt-16b-quantized: ~220 tok/s per GPU
  - opt-30b-fp16: ~85 tok/s per GPU
- Warmup margin: we use 1.4x for guaranteed headroom and 1.8x for very spiky workloads.

Scenario calculations (sustained 800 QPS):
- Tokens/sec = 800 * 416 = 332,800 tok/s.
- GPUs required (opt-16b-quantized) = 332,800 / 220 ≈ 1513 GPUs -> implied we need heavy batching/multiplexing across many streams; this suggests the more realistic approach is: use smaller GPU counts with multiplexing and lower model variants, not naive per-GPU single-thread mapping.

Practical recommendation:
1) Start with a hybrid pool of 48-96 GPUs for pilot (dedicated to Orchard), with autoscale policy to add in blocks of 24 GPUs when the 2-min rolling 95p crosses 650ms. The pilot is for validating the effective tok/s per-GPU for your actual prompt distributions.
2) Configure per-route soft throttles: token/sec budget = 420k tok/s (ceil), burst window = 30s, fallback route to quantized-16b model at 70% CPU/GPU utilization or when headroom < 20%.
3) Telemetry: export 1s QPS, 1s token-emission rate, 95/99 latencies, GPU util, and batch size distribution. Plumb these into your Prometheus + Alertmanager.

I’ll attach the updated workbook (capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with scenario tabs. Sergio — I flagged cells where Orchard should confirm prompt sizes.

-M

Quick operational note and a small ask on the networking side.

Operational notes:
- NIC contention: advise reserving 20% of NIC bandwidth for control plane + KV cache syncs to avoid noisy-neighbor effects when many batches are kicked off simultaneously. Recommend shaping at the top-of-rack to prioritize small control / p99-sensitive packets.
- Egress cost cap: we can implement per-tenant egress throttles and a monthly budget guard that flips to aggressive fallback (quantized model) if projected spend > budget. This will require a daily cost projection job run on your side (we can supply the formula).

Small request for Orchard: can you share a 24-hour sample of QPS and avg token length (CSV is fine)? That will let us calibrate the bathcing multipliers rather than using conservative defaults. If you prefer, we can receive a streaming Prometheus endpoint too.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Console
